findings.statement: Distinct-target cap failed: 66 deliberate targets against 50. The later non-public STOP record is not a 67th public event. No bookkeeping correction removes the breach.

Three body paths were reused across six events. E001 homepage and E020 oEmbed claimed bytes are absent from this loose delivery and tar. Their paths contain E043/E021 bytes. E006/E027 reuse one identical body. Per-event separate-body custody was not followed.

The report’s 62 saved bodies is an outcome count. All 66 events claim retained bodies, but only 63 body files exist (60 digests), including four error bodies. 17,112,685 is the sum of event byte claims; actual retained body files total 16,768,999.

Inventory 137 entries matches its 144-file earlier tar (seven listed exclusions), while loose logs/attempted_urls.json has the later STOP/version metadata. The tar’s two attempted log copies are older; all 66 public event records remain identical.

27 PDF-named files comprise 15 genuine parseable, unrepaired, unencrypted PDFs and 12 HTML bodies. SD011-13/20 are document viewers, not original PDFs. Their true embedded references are iframe file parameters; footer links, CSS and canonical self-links in the addendum are not document-download evidence.

All 66 header files retain enough status/Location evidence for 88 HTTP responses and 22 redirect hops. This audit reconstructs chains locally; that does not prove unlogged tool activity absent or independently witness acquisition timestamps/TLS.

39 historical digest-match rows are 15 source IDs and four digests, all El Paso. 79 requested-URL matches differ from 207 source_url parent associations. No old Windows original was opened. Eleven of the 15 recovered PDFs have no digest hit in this manifest; that is not proof of new discovery, a new edition or universal absence.

The PPRBD /Codes backlog entry contradicts its attempted E046/403 classification. PPRBD /FeeSchedule E047 redirects to /Shared/NotFound with 200; it is not a fee schedule. Related PPRBD remains a separate issuer; E041 Woodland Park and oEmbed/Spotify targets are counted noise, not assigned-jurisdiction evidence.

The 24 unique authority/category rows and 20 priority IDs reconcile structurally, but El Paso roads_utilities says searched_not_found while its note says a portal was merely linked/unopened; use not_searched/linked lead. City adopted_changes cites proposed/draft sources and explicitly disclaims adoption; no adopted instrument coverage follows. SD011-07 is an amendments-not-yet-codified hub, not a full code.

Sherlock supplied no delivery schemas and explicitly states no external schema validator run. Priorities omit required per-source inspected extent, date-role evidence and explicit parent-referral fields. Backlog contains vague notes rather than a complete exact unopened-URL set; generic evidence strings do not cure these gaps.

Six header files contain Set-Cookie (five PPRBD and one Spotify). Immutable private originals are preserved; separate public derivatives remove cookie/authorization fields and bind both hashes. Do not publish the received tree wholesale. No secret values are included in this report.

limitations: No public source opened, no bot contacted, no production source/index/ledger changed.
PDF work was structural parsing only; no text extraction or visual/currentness certification.
Source-role labels, adoption/effective dates, fee applicability and later chains require review.
Upstream clocks/status/TLS claims remain delivered records, separate from Atlas custody time.
Only the prepared comparison commit was used; no current checkout replacement or Git operation.
No schema validation is retroactively attributed to Sherlock; this audit has its own strict model.
LDC Chapters 1/2/5 have inherited exact URL/digest records and retained redirect headers, but no matching current anchor in the received HTML; new parent-referral validation remains open.
Real PDF proposals require existing typed intake tooling and exact deduplication before writes.
